newsitem.title: USA: Clarence Kelley, former FBI director, dies at 85.
newsitem.headline: Clarence Kelley, former FBI director, dies at 85.

text.p: Former FBI Director Clarence Kelley, 85, died Tuesday in his home after a long illness, Jeff Lanza, a special agent with the bureau in Kansas City, said.
Kelley was director of the FBI from July 1973 to February 1978.
Before becoming director, he was chief of police of Kansas City, Missouri. He was an FBI agent from 1940 to 1961.

In Washington the current director, Louis J. Freeh, said in a statement: "Clarence Kelley represented the best of the FBI -- the past and future. He served his country and the law enforcement community unselfishly and distinguished himself in a variety of assignments throughout his career. ...

"During Kelley's tenure as director, the FBI made a strong effort to develop an agent force with more women and one that was more reflective of the ethnic composition of the United States, as well as (establishing) three national priorities: foreign counterintelligence, organised crime and white-collar crime."
Kelley is survived by his wife, a son, a daughter and three grandchildren.
Funeral services will be held Friday at the Country Club Christian Church in Kansas City, Lanza said.
